events.ai_basis: Exceptions to this fixed procedure include work on a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function and proof of the Hodge Conjecture for CM abelian varieties.

why: The statement is the full rational Hodge conjecture for every smooth complex projective variety. So every restricted-class result is a case: CM abelian varieties, Weil-type fourfolds, K3 families and resolutions of A_n hypersurfaces. Markman's sixfold/fourfold result is marked digested, which is a close call. Totaro's named guest post is an expository digest of the argument, and Voisin's status survey treats it as established. Under F9 that clears the bar, though neither says they checked every line. Floccari-Fu and Floccari are marked digested on the authors' 'final version, to appear' journal comments. The OpenAI CM claim (in both its own event and the bundled openai-math-032) is case, unreviewed and doubtful rather than not_credible. Sister papers were withdrawn and the split-Weil dependency is unresolved, but no specific error in the CM argument has been identified. Its AI role is generated: the README says the repository's manuscripts were produced by an internal OpenAI model, and the only author is OpenAI. The README's statement that the CM result was an 'exception to this fixed procedure' leaves open how it was produced, but nothing in it credits a human. The full-proof claims from Bouali, Shimizu, the Zenodo records and Oo each carry several F10 signals. The integral-conjecture disproof and OpenAI's characteristic-p specialization result are variants. Jumagulov's finite Fermat list is instances. The withdrawn papers are knocked down.
doubts: First, the CM manuscript appears as two events (openai-cm-rational-hodge-2026 and the bundled openai-math-032); I answered them consistently. Second, its AI role rests on a repository-wide README quote, and the README calls this result an exception to the standard procedure without explaining what the exception was; human involvement could be larger than the generated answer assumes. Third, journal acceptances for Floccari-Fu and Floccari rest only on the authors' arXiv comments. Fourth, Markman's 'digested' turns on reading Totaro's expository post as a digested rewrite.
